stories.headline_en: US Jury Convicts Huawei of Trade Secret Theft but Rejects Racketeering
stories.summary_en: A federal jury in Brooklyn has found Chinese telecommunications giant Huawei guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud following a two-month trial. However, jurors acquitted the company of the more serious overarching racketeering conspiracy charge, which required proving the firm operated as a criminal enterprise. Huawei stated it intends to appeal the convictions while noting the racketeering acquittal repudiated the prosecution's central allegations.
stories.why_en: The landmark verdict concludes years of federal legal action targeting Huawei's operations while rejecting prosecutors' broadest claims that the company functioned as an illicit racketeering organisation.

sources.title: China’s Huawei found guilty of trade secrets conspiracy, fraud in US trial
Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering

stories.headline_en: US Attorney General Defends Nvidia but Dodges Questions on Huang Investigation
stories.summary_en: US Attorney General Todd Blanche has described Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to confirm whether reinstated chief executive Jensen Huang was ever under federal investigation. Huang resigned after revelations of extramarital relationships, including one with an executive at customer firm Megaspeed who was an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, before being reinstated following encouragement from President Donald Trump. Lawmakers from both parties have raised national security concerns and pledged congressional investigations
stories.why_en: The situation has triggered bipartisan political backlash in Washington over executive branch intervention in corporate leadership and the enforcement of technology export controls.

sources.title: Todd Blanche declines to confirm if Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was investigated
US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation

stories.headline_en: UK Announces Independent Panel on Health Impact of Cold War Nuclear Tests
stories.summary_en: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ordered an independent panel to investigate the long-term health consequences of the UK's Cold War-era nuclear weapons testing in the 1950s and 1960s. Modelled on the Hillsborough inquiry and led by former Bishop James Jones, the panel will assess claims from surviving veterans and their descendants regarding radiation-induced illnesses. The Ministry of Defence previously cited studies showing no increased health risks, but campaigners have long alleged the withholding of key medical records.
stories.why_en: The decision marks a major step forward for surviving veterans and family campaigns that have sought official transparency and accountability for more than seven decades.

sources.title: Nuclear test veterans will get full truth, says Burnham, as he confirms independent panel
Nuclear test veterans speak to BBC about search for justice

stories.headline_en: Welsh Government Rules Out Mass Badger Cull in Bovine TB Strategy
stories.summary_en: The Welsh government has ruled out a mass cull of badgers as part of updated plans to eradicate bovine tuberculosis, adopting an evidence-based approach focused on cattle testing, farm movement controls, and targeted wildlife research. Although nearly 96% of cattle herds in Wales are disease-free, more than 10,000 cattle were slaughtered following TB testing over the past year. Farming groups urged rapid implementation of targeted measures, while wildlife organisations welcomed the exclusion of a blanket cull.
stories.why_en: The announcement resolves months of debate across Wales by seeking a compromise between agricultural disease control and wildlife protection standards.

sources.title: Badger cull ruled out by Welsh government after speculation

stories.headline_en: Real Madrid Overcome Deficit to Defeat PSV 5-1 in Champions League
stories.summary_en: Real Madrid recovered from a 1-0 half-time deficit to defeat PSV 5-1 at the Santiago Bernabeu, preserving a perfect record in the Champions League league phase. After Ivan Perisic scored a first-half penalty for PSV, second-half substitute Jude Bellingham sparked Madrid's turnaround with a volleyed goal and an assist. Kylian Mbappe scored twice, alongside goals from Federico Valverde and Vinicius Junior, securing Madrid's tenth consecutive win across all competitions.
stories.why_en: The victory keeps Real Madrid provisionally top of the Champions League league phase standings with five wins from five matches.

sources.title: Bellingham stunner, Mbappe brace help Real Madrid rout PSV
